# test/fixtures/UpdateFlowTest.java
- Lines: 2225 | Kind: transplant + host-JVM integration (92 scenario methods run from `main`, compiled against members that `exactUpdateMembers` in `specs/quint/refinement/native/update-barrier.mjs` slices out of `AlphaDevicePlugin.java`, plus the stubs in `test/fixtures/app-update-jvm/`); also the shared support library of three live Quint native harnesses | Verdict: KEEP the support helpers, SIMPLIFY the scenarios (delete the legacy-build cases), PORT with the update-flow extraction (T10)
- Covers: one-tap and automatic self-update. A download is admitted only at its declared size and SHA-256. Each process makes at most one install attempt, fenced by the PackageInstaller session and its binding. The confirmation is kept for the requesting bridge and survives restart. The draft-flush and shutdown barrier come before the commit. Automatic mode admits only when the app is foreground, unlocked, idle and the user has consented. A verified cache is retried over real loopback TLS.
- Duplicates: `specs/quint/refinement/native/UpdateBarrierHarness.java`, `UpdateStagingHarness.java` and `UpdateCompositionHarness.java` (with `update-barrier.mjs`, `update-staging.mjs`, `update-composition.mjs`) drive the same members through this class's helpers. `test/app-update.test.mjs` tests 1, 3 and 4 are source-text checks around it. Device evidence comes from the emulator instrumentation tests.
- Callers/importers: `test/app-update.test.mjs:42` compiles and runs it (`main`, 240 s timeout, keytool keystore argument for the TLS case). The Quint harnesses call the static helpers `installing`, `bridge`, `offered`, `committed`, `confirmation`, `dismissed`, `retireFixtureWorkers` and `serveFixtureHttps`, and reach `forgetProcess` by reflection (`UpdateCompositionHarness.java:232`, `UpdateStagingHarness.java:169`). `update-staging.mjs:152`, `update-composition.mjs:27` and `update-barrier.mjs:15` list the file as a compile input. **Correction:** `files/test/app-update.test.mjs.md` says this file is "used only here". That is wrong: deleting `app-update.test.mjs` does not free it.

## Findings
| # | Lines | Pattern | Finding | Change | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 938-953, 1246-1248 | A1 | `aSessionBoundWithoutTheIntentMarkFencesUntilABoot` and the "binding an earlier build wrote without the mark" case test sessions that builds 93f630662..fd5e9d09c7 left behind. They back the optional `(/intent)?` group in `AlphaDevicePlugin.UPDATE_BINDING` (product line 293, comments at 294, 694, 735). PackageInstaller sessions belong to the installing package, and the renamed package has no sessions from those builds. | Delete both cases together with the optional group and its comment branches in the product. Unmarked bindings then parse as unknown, and unknown fences. | Medium: owner confirmation is needed, because this is device-level installer state (compare D17). |
| 2 | 914-937, 1062-1077, 1192-1213 | A1, T4 | `anUnboundUnsealedSessionFencesLikeASealedOne` ("what the published 2bdb15408b leaves"), `sealedSessionsEachHoldUntilAndroidEndsThem` ("an older build could leave one sealed session per bridge") and `anUnknownSessionStaysFenced` are named after legacy builds. Their behaviour, that unknown means fence, is generic and `aCorruptBindingFencesRatherThanClears` (1214) already covers it for sealed and unsealed sessions. | Delete the first two. Keep the rule by adding a `null` referrer to the `broken` list at 1218, and keep one restored-after-reboot sdk loop from `anUnknownSessionStaysFenced`. | Low |
| 3 | 200-213, 224-228 | D7, T2 | `forgetProcess` and `plugin(...)` reset 20 private static fields of `AlphaDevicePlugin` by reflection (`activation`, `updateResume`, `updating`, `UPDATE_DEADLINE_NANOS` …), so each rename breaks this class and three harnesses. | When the update flow is extracted from `AlphaDevicePlugin` into a plain `AppUpdateFlow` instance with injected installer, HTTP and clock ports (proposed in `app-update.test.mjs.md`), replace these helpers with `new AppUpdateFlow(...)` per scenario and a real clock port. | Medium (large refactor) |
| 4 | 35-42, whole file | T10 | The class compiles against a text slice (`exactUpdateMembers`) of the product class, not the product class itself, and the slice is cut at literal member names. | PORT: the harnesses and this test compile the real extracted class. The product needs a package-private `AppUpdateFlow` exposing `install`, `activate`, `continueUpdate`, `state`, `onStatus` and `onResume`/`onDestroy` hooks. | Medium |
| 5 | 44-233 vs 235-2108 | C5, D11 | Shared harness support (fixtures, fakes, `installing`, `bridge`, `offered`, TLS server) and 92 scenarios sit in one 2.2k-line file, and the Quint harnesses import a class named "…Test". | Split into `UpdateFixture.java` (helpers, used by the harnesses) and `UpdateFlowScenarios.java`. Move both next to their main consumer, under `specs/quint/refinement/native/` or `test/support/android-update/`. | Low |
| 6 | 940, 956, 988, 1028, 1037, 1080, 1102, 1171, 1194, ... | runtime | About 15 scenarios loop sdk 29..37 or 38 (×codename ×phase), so a few thousand Context and bridge setups each retire worker executors (20 s bound). This is the main cost of the 240 s JVM run. | Keep the sdk loops only where the product branches on the level (31/32, 34, 36). Run boundary levels {29, 30, 31, 33, 34, 36, 37} instead of every level. | Low: the product's sdk branches are explicit. |

| 8 | 1757 | T8 | `Thread.sleep(50)` is used to show that "nothing happens". | Keep it. It is a bounded negative check and the cheapest available. You could also assert on the worker queue instead. | Low |

## Proposed end state
- `UpdateFixture.java` (about 230 lines of helpers) serves the three Quint native update harnesses and the scenario file.
- The scenario file loses findings 1-2 (about 90 lines) and trims its sdk loops to boundary levels.
- After the `AppUpdateFlow` extraction, the reflection resets and the text slice go away. Every consumer compiles the real class.
- This stays the deepest host check of one-tap update. It is not Android evidence, as its header already says.
